metadata.case_name: HO CHI KIN v. CHAN HOI SHING

plaintiff.expected_occupation_after: alternative employment when he attained the age of 50 years

injuries.description: trochanteric fracture of the right femur
source: As a result of the fall, the plaintiff had a trochanteric fracture of the right femur, spent a period in hospital and while he has now returned to his same job as a tally clerk, is in receipt of a reduced income.
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of trochanteric section of femur

manifestations.description: The operation has left an 8 inch scar.
There has been wasting of the thigh muscles
10 degree loss of rotation of the leg
8% impairment of the leg or 5% of the whole man
he did not now accept work on ships which involved excessive climbing; even on those ships which he now boarded the arrangement with his employer is that he no longer climbs stacked cargo
pain, suffering and loss of amenities

treatments_received: On 2nd June 1983 he was operated on when a bone plate was inserted secured with an angled prong and five bone screws.
Readmitted into hospital on 6th March 1985 for removal of the bone plate and screws.

losses.description: 8% impairment of the leg or 5% of the whole man; permanent disabilities affecting employment
The operation has left an 8 inch scar.
10 degree loss of rotation of the leg; wasting of the thigh muscles; inability to perform climbing duties aboard ships
